top_signals.title: Theater in Abu Dhabi, Everyday Life at Home: Why the War Still Shapes Every Story
top_signals.summary:
Welcome to The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest of Ukrainian commentary and analysis from across the political spectrum, only for War on the Rocks members. Each week, we bring you a curated selection of articles from Ukrainian media offering insight into how Ukrainians themselves debate the issues shaping their country.Western coverage often narrows the view to the battlefield — these pieces widen it, revealing the texture of daily life, politics, and public argument in a nation at war. The perspectives gathered here are varied, candid, and often surprising, together forming a more complete picture of Ukraine as it really is.Frontline

top_signals.title: Iraq's Border Shutdown With Iran Threatens a Much Bigger Economic Crisis
top_signals.summary: Iraq’s closure of the Al-Sheeb crossing with Iran is less an economic rupture than a test of whether Baghdad can secure its borders without damaging its economy. The immediate costs are concentrated in Maysan Province and are manageable, at least for now. A wider, prolonged shutdown would be different: it would disrupt trade, raise costs for Iraqi businesses and consumers, and complicate Baghdad’s effort to establish Iraq as a regional transportation and logistics hub. top_signals.title: U.S. natural gas inventories end injection season above normal levels
top_signals.summary: Working natural gas in storage in the Lower 48 states ended the natural gas injection season at 3,810 billion cubic feet (Bcf), exceeding the five-year average by almost 2%, according to estimates based on data from our Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report released on November 12. Injection season runs April 1–October 31, the months of typically lower natural gas demand.
